page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system features a shared CPU allocation model under KVM virtualization. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.0 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by three NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 144 GB of VRAM.

In benchmark evaluations, this server demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics. Memory bandwidth is strong, ranking in the top 25% with read-only cached speeds of 6377.89 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 123.17 GB/sec. Large language model inference speeds for prompt processing and text generation using 135M and 7B models also rank in the top 10%, with the 7B model achieving 6061.83 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 129.38 tokens/sec for text generation.

A key architectural tradeoff of this instance is the absence of local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be handled externally. Additionally, the CPU allocation is shared rather than dedicated. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of GPU resources and system memory relative to the 32 vCPUs provides a specialized hardware profile designed to maximize parallel processing throughput per resource unit.

This server configuration is designed for workloads such as large language model inference, machine learning training, ray tracing, and complex database operations. The combination of high-capacity GPU VRAM and top-tier CPU decompression and physics performance also makes it suitable for parallel data processing and scientific simulations.
